name: 博扬·暮耕
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:1469
who: Bojan Duskplough, a human contract farmer of Wheatshed village just west of the boundary stones on the long wall, grandson of a family carried off over the wall generations ago, twenty-one in the autumn the wheat burned: tall, about 181 cm, long-boned and broad-shouldered with long arms. Stiff black hair cut short, with a blue sheen in sunlight; an untidy stubble on the chin; thick dark brows; deep blue eyes that look first at whether a person's back is bent. Since the fire both palms have been a layer of shiny hard scar, and his left forearm bears a round scar on each side where a musket ball went through. His back is always ramrod straight. A blunt, stubborn, quick-tempered air that cools slowly.
build: 181 cm, long-boned: broad shoulders, long arms and a lean, very straight back.
palette: undyed linen and wheat gold, deep blue, soot grey, worn leather brown
casual: His contract-folk clothes: a coarse undyed linen shirt with the sleeves rolled above the elbow, a hemp-rope belt with a small wooden tag hanging from it, branded with his family's contract number, rough brown trousers and worn boots; slung across his chest a cloth bag of seed grain that was his grandfather's; strips of cloth wound loosely round both scarred palms against the cold. He holds a sickle whose wooden handle is worn shiny, standing very straight, a blunt, unsmiling look.
private: At home in Wheatshed on a winter evening: a loose undyed linen shirt, the plain grey wool coat issued to the contract-folk each winter thrown over his shoulders, rough trousers, bare feet. One hand is pushed deep into the cloth seed bag at his hip to warm the scarred palm. A quiet, stubborn half-smile.
battle: Cutting a firebreak: the linen shirt streaked with soot, a wet cloth knotted round his neck ready to pull over his mouth, cloth strips wound round both palms, the wooden tag at his belt, the seed bag across his chest. He grips a long-handled iron hoe in both hands, its blade dark with earth.
battle_pose: 3) the firebreak outfit: braced and determined, the feet planted wide, a fierce, scowling expression, gripping a long-handled iron hoe in both hands as if about to cut a trench; he does not fight.
formal: Speaking for his village at the border officer's table: the grey wool winter coat issued under the contract, brushed clean and buttoned up over a clean linen shirt, the wooden contract tag on its cord outside the coat, the hair combed down, clean boots. He stands very straight with the hands at his sides, a stubborn, serious look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the deep blue eyes looking straight at the viewer from under thick brows, unbending, a small stable lantern raised in one scarred hand. Warm orange lantern light from one side against a dusky blue sky. Foreground blur: ripe wheat ears, drifting ash and the grey edge of a boundary stone. He wears the coarse linen shirt with the seed bag across his chest.

name: 哈迪雅·赤脊
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:1525
who: Hadiya Redridge, a fire-horn demon-kin woman of the old Redridge clan and a contract judge of the black empire who walks the border lands reading burnt ground, ninety-one and looking twenty-seven or twenty-eight: tall, about 179 cm, slender. Charcoal-grey skin, warm to the touch like all her folk. A pair of dark red horns sweeping back from the brow, their tips gone black. Black hair in one tight braid down her back. Amber eyes that look at a person's hands first. All ten fingertips ash-white, the ash worked into the whorls for good. On her chest, on a leather cord, the two halves of an iron ring sawn apart, the cut edges blackened: her grandfather's blood-oath ring. A slow, exact, patient air; she says nothing she has not checked in the ash.
face: FACE, as in the references: a young woman's face of about twenty-seven, calm and exact: medium, gently slanted almond eyes of amber with a level, searching gaze and a thin tapering upper lash line; straight black brows; a closed, unhurried mouth. Charcoal-grey skin with very little shading, the skin shadows a soft cool slate.
build: 179 cm, tall and slender: a medium bust, a narrow waist and full hips, long legs.
palette: judge's black and cord red, charcoal grey, ash white, amber
casual: Her contract judge's clothes: a long black coat buttoned to the collar with a single red cord at the collar, its hem always grey with ash, dark trousers and soft boots for kneeling; at her waist a leather pouch holding a book full of drawn fires and several small cloth bags of ash; the two halves of the sawn iron ring on their leather cord at her chest. She holds a pinch of ash between two whitened fingertips, a slow, appraising look.
private: At home in the border city after a long walk: a loose undyed linen shirt with the sleeves rolled, a long dark wool skirt, soft shoes, the braid over one shoulder. She holds the two halves of the iron ring in her open palm, a thumb running over the sawn edge. A tired, inward look.
battle: At a fire site: the black coat belted close and its hem tucked up, leather knee pads, a scarf hanging at her neck ready to tie over her nose and mouth, the pouch of ash bags at her waist. She holds an open book of drawn fires in one hand and a stick of charcoal in the other.
battle_pose: 3) the field outfit: alert and steady, the feet a little apart on burnt ground, a level, searching expression, holding an open book of drawn fires in one hand and a stick of charcoal in the other; she carries no weapon.
formal: Sitting in judgement at the contract court: the long black coat brushed clean and buttoned to the throat, the red cord at the collar, a dark red sash, polished boots, the braid pinned up behind the horns, the two halves of the ring on their cord outside the coat. She stands very upright with the hands folded in front, a grave, exact look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the amber eyes looking up at the viewer from under the dark red horns, two ash-white fingertips raised near her lips with a pinch of ash she is about to taste. Low red-orange ember light from one side. Foreground blur: drifting grey ash flakes, a few sparks and the two sawn halves of an iron ring on a cord. She wears the long black judge's coat with the red cord at the collar.

name: 格拉德
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:1697
who: Glad, a half-orc of the Rut-Stone valley, this person in an earlier period: once the Charred-Gate clan's first hammer who broke fourteen village gates, then thirty years in the Thunder Gaol, now a cobbler at the gate of Rutmouth; seventy-two, a legend since the dawn on the grey ridge, looking forty-five or forty-six ever since. About 205 cm, huge and heavy, his back like a slab pried off a cliff. Grey-green skin. Short messy dark brown hair going grey at the temples, a short stubble beard, calm brown eyes that look first at what a person is holding. Fourteen small black iron shards grown into the skin of his shoulders and upper back, a few showing at the collar; long surgical scars up both forearms. A slow, heavy, quiet air; he keeps his hands where people can see them.
face: FACE, as in the references: a weathered half-orc man's face of about forty-five, broad and heavy-boned, NOT young: calm brown eyes under a heavy brow, a few lines at their corners; a broad nose; a set, closed mouth; two short lower tusks rising past the upper lip, the left chipped at one corner, the right broken off halfway; a short stubble beard and a thin scar across one cheek. Grey-green skin with very little shading, skin shadows a soft cool olive.
build: 205 cm, huge and heavy: very broad shoulders, a thick back, forearms thicker than most men's legs.
palette: ash grey and grey-green, charred black, worn leather brown, a faint ember red
casual: His cobbler's clothes by the town gate: a coarse undyed cloth coat with the sleeves rolled to the elbows, both scarred forearms bare, a plain shirt under it, heavy trousers and worn boots; both fists wrapped from the knuckles to the wrists in cloth bands charred black; at his waist a leather bag holding an awl, waxed thread and a roll of cured leather. Both big hands rest open at his sides where they can be seen, a calm, guarded look.
private: Mending boots under his lean-to by the gate: the coat off, a loose undyed linen shirt with the sleeves rolled up, the charred fist bands, heavy trousers. He holds a worn boot and an awl threaded with waxed thread, about to put in one more stitch. A quiet, tired half-smile.
battle: Standing between someone and a falling blow: the coarse coat belted tight, the sleeves rolled, the forearm scars showing, fresh cloth bands on both fists already charring, a short iron chain with a clasp hooked at his belt.
battle_pose: 3) the battle outfit: braced and immovable, the feet planted wide and the knees a little bent, both wrapped fists raised in a closed guard before the chest as if to catch a falling blow, not striking, a grim, steady look; he carries no weapon.
formal: His one clean coat: a long plain dark grey wool coat buttoned to the top button, as worn before the contract court, dark trousers and boots he resoled himself, the fist bands freshly wound but already charred. He stands upright with both big hands open at his sides, a careful, humble look.
art: A portrait from slightly below with the camera tilted, the face large, the brown eyes looking at the viewer steadily over one raised fist wrapped in charred cloth, the half-broken tusk showing in a set mouth. Cold grey dawn light from one side, a faint red glow rising from behind his shoulder. Foreground blur: drifting ash, the links of a heavy iron chain and the toe of a mended boot. He wears the coarse cloth coat with the sleeves rolled.

name: 苏海拉
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:1758
who: Suhaila, a fire-horn demon-kin woman of the Horn-Crown house of the Charred-Gate clan, the clan's hammer-warden, who climbed the grey ridge every night for five years to oil the chain of the great gate hammer, nineteen: tall, about 176 cm, slender, with shoulders, back and arms made strong by hauling chain. Skin with a faint red cast. Two horns sweeping back from the temples, a ring of black obsidian clasped round each horn root, the mark of her house, the tips scorched black. Dark red hair with singed black ends, in one thick braid coiled at the back of her head. Red-gold eyes that look first at what is holding a thing up. Ring-shaped old marks around both forearms and two dark red scars where a chain once tore the skin. A steady, hard, few-worded air.
face: FACE, as in the references: a young woman's face of about nineteen, steady and unsmiling: medium, gently slanted almond eyes of red-gold with a level gaze and a thin tapering upper lash line; straight dark red brows; a firm, closed mouth; a neat, strong chin. Clean skin with a faint warm red cast and very little shading; skin shadows a soft warm red-brown.
build: 176 cm, tall and slender with strong shoulders, back and arms: a small bust, a narrow waist and gently rounded hips.
palette: charred black and ember red, obsidian black, red gold, iron grey
casual: Her hammer-warden's clothes: a short black leather jacket of the Charred-Gate clan, the cuffs clasped shut with iron rings so a chain cannot catch them, dark trousers and sturdy boots with heavy hand-stitched soles, worn-thin leather hand guards on both hands; a length of broken heavy chain wound several times round her waist. She holds the loose end of the chain in one hand, a steady, watchful look.
private: In the mountains after she left the clan: a plain undyed linen shirt with the cuffs tied, a dark wool vest, dark trousers and the stitched boots, the braid hanging over one shoulder. She holds the broken chain across her palms, wiping it link by link with a cloth. A quiet, tired look.
battle: On the slope below the grey ridge: the black leather jacket buckled tight, the iron-ringed cuffs, the leather hand guards, the chain unwound from her waist. She grips the heavy broken chain in both hands, a length of it swinging low and ready to throw, a hard, steady look.
formal: Before the contract court in the horn city: a long dark grey wool coat buttoned to the top button, as worn before the court, the obsidian rings on her horns, the broken chain still wound at her waist. She stands very upright with the hands folded in front, a grave, unflinching look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the red-gold eyes looking at the viewer steadily, both hands gripping a taut heavy chain close beside her face. Cold grey dawn light from one side over a ridge of ash. Foreground blur: big iron chain links, drifting ash and the black head of an iron nail. She wears the short black leather jacket with the iron-ringed cuffs.

name: 嘉尔娜
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:1816
who: Jarna, a half-orc woman of the Rut-Stone valley, granddaughter of the valley's keeper of the genealogy and now its keeper herself; at eight she was the youngest of the six children tied in the gate on the grey ridge, and she is drawn here grown, at twenty-six: very tall, about 191 cm, broad-shouldered and thick-backed. Grey-brown skin. Unruly moss-green hair in two thick braids. Orange-yellow eyes that look straight at people. Two small lower tusks, one with a chipped corner from biting through a rope. On her left wrist a frayed rope end, tied on and never untied. A blunt, loud, fearless air; the first thing she asks anyone is their name and their mother's name.
face: FACE, as in the references: a young half-orc woman's face of about twenty-six, broad and strong, NOT delicate: medium almond eyes of orange-yellow, wide open and direct, with a thin tapering upper lash line; thick moss-green brows; a broad nose; a wide mouth with two small lower tusks showing at its corners, one chipped. Grey-brown skin with very little shading, skin shadows a soft warm umber.
build: 191 cm, very tall and strong: broad shoulders, a thick back and a sturdy frame.
palette: moss green and grey-brown, orange-yellow, undyed wool, a little faded rope red
casual: Her keeper's clothes in the valley: a coarse undyed wool tunic to the knees, belted with a leather strap, over dark trousers and heavy boots; at her waist a leather pouch holding a few chisels and a genealogy she copied by hand onto a roll of cured leather; the frayed rope end on her left wrist. She holds the leather roll in one hand, a loud, open look.
private: In the stone hut where the valley's genealogy is kept: a loose undyed linen shirt with the sleeves rolled, a long dark brown wool skirt, soft boots, the braids loose. She holds an old roll of cured leather open in both hands, reading it under her breath. A quiet, absorbed look.
battle: On the ridge, calling names: a sheepskin-lined leather jerkin over the tunic, leather bracers, the pouch of chisels at her waist, heavy boots. She holds the rolled genealogy in one hand and cups the other at her mouth.
battle_pose: 3) the field outfit: braced and ready, the feet planted wide, a fierce, open expression, one hand cupped at her mouth as if about to shout a name across a valley, the other holding a rolled leather genealogy; she does not fight.
formal: On the day she carved the names on the back of the stele: a long clean dark moss-green wool coat buttoned to the collar, a leather sash, a chisel and mallet at her belt, the braids freshly tied with leather thongs, the rope end still on her wrist. She stands very upright with the hands folded in front, a serious, proud look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the orange-yellow eyes looking straight at the viewer, the mouth open mid-shout with one hand cupped beside it. Warm low sunset light from one side over a stone valley. Foreground blur: drifting dust, the frayed rope end on her wrist and the corner of a rolled leather genealogy. She wears the coarse undyed wool tunic with the leather pouch.

name: 嘉尔娜
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:1816
who: Jarna as a child, a half-orc girl of the Rut-Stone valley and granddaughter of the valley's keeper of the genealogy, eight years old in the autumn she was the youngest of the six children tied in the gate on the grey ridge: a head taller than human children of her age, about 131 cm, wholly covered by her clothes. Grey-brown skin and a round face. Messy moss-green hair in two short pigtails. Orange-yellow eyes that look straight at people. Two tiny lower tusks just showing past her lip, one with a corner chipped from biting through a rope. A frayed rope end tied round her left wrist. A loud, blunt, fearless air; she does not cry, she asks how many more days.
face: FACE, as in the references: a half-orc child's face of about eight, round and bright: large, round orange-yellow eyes with a thin tapering upper lash line; short moss-green brows; a small broad nose; a wide mouth with two tiny lower tusks just showing at its corners, one chipped; soft round cheeks. Grey-brown skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft warm umber.
palette: moss green and grey-brown, orange-yellow, undyed homespun, frayed rope beige
casual: Her valley clothes: a short coarse homespun tunic with long sleeves, belted with a cord, over plain leggings, bare feet; the frayed rope end tied on her left wrist. She stands with her chin up and her small fists clenched at her sides, a loud, curious look.
private: At home in the stone hut of the genealogy: a long undyed wool shift with long sleeves, a knitted shawl round her shoulders, the pigtails loose. She hugs a rolled leather genealogy almost as long as her arm. A sleepy, contented look.
battle: The dawn in the gate: the short homespun tunic, bare feet, dust on her knees, the bitten rope end on her wrist.
battle_pose: 3) the outfit of that dawn: standing straight, the feet planted, a fierce, unafraid expression, one hand cupped at her mouth as if calling out a name, the other a small fist at her side; she does not fight.
formal: In the spring after the gate: a clean homespun dress to the shins with long sleeves, a small leather vest, her first pair of boots, resoled by Glad, the pigtails neatly tied. She stands very straight with the hands clasped in front, a proud, serious look.
art: A head-and-shoulders portrait, the face turned slightly, the orange-yellow eyes looking straight at the viewer, the mouth open as if about to ask how many more days. Cold grey dawn light from one side. Foreground blur: drifting ash and a frayed rope end. She wears the coarse homespun tunic, closed at the collar.

name: 吕迪格·鸢羽
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:2004
who: Rudiger Kitefeather, a human knight of the new dynasty, third son of the Kitefeather house, nineteen and serving his year on the long wall at Storkbridge: about 183 cm, shot up fast, thin and long-armed, his frame not yet filled out, so his eldest brother's old half-plate sits a finger too big on him. Sandy-gold hair cut very short; pale gold eyes that look far off first and near second; the bridge of the nose sunburnt red and peeling. A grey-white kite feather stands in the crest of his helm. On his back a round white shield rimmed with iron, its face left blank until he earns something worth painting on it. A warm, eager, talkative air; he knows every song of the wall by heart.
build: 183 cm, tall and lanky: shoulders not yet broad, long arms, a young rider's straight back.
palette: kite white and iron grey, sandy gold, pale gold, a little dark blue
casual: His wall-service dress: the Kitefeather house's white surcoat with a single kite feather embroidered at the collar, over his eldest brother's half-plate, its pauldrons a finger too big and lashed tight with leather thongs; dark trousers and riding boots; a leather wallet at his belt stuffed with unanswered letters from home; the blank white round shield rimmed with iron on his back; the open-faced helm with the grey-white kite feather hooked at his belt. He holds his family's heirloom lance with its grey tassel slanted low beside him, an eager, open look.
private: Off duty in the wall barracks: a loose cream linen shirt with the sleeves pushed up, a brown wool waistcoat, dark trousers and boots, no armour. He holds a folded letter from his mother, still sealed, turning it over in his hands. A wistful, boyish look.
battle: Holding a gateway: the white surcoat over the oversized half-plate, the open-faced helm with the grey-white kite feather on his head, leather gauntlets, the blank white round shield on his left arm. He holds the heirloom lance with its grey tassel low and angled forward in his right hand, a tense, determined look.
formal: In the hall of his family's house in the golden-kite city: a long white wool coat with a single kite feather embroidered at the collar, a dark blue sash, white gloves, polished riding boots, the hair combed flat. He stands very straight with one gloved hand on the hilt of a plain sword, a serious, slightly nervous look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the pale gold eyes turning from the far distance to the viewer, the sunburnt nose and an eager, half-open mouth as if about to ask a question. Warm low evening sun from one side over a battlement. Foreground blur: the iron rim of the blank white shield, a drifting grey-white feather and the far dots of many campfires. He wears the white surcoat with the embroidered kite feather.

name: 茉妲·雨行
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:2061
who: Moda Rainwalk, a tiefling of the black empire, seventh generation of a family who left the burning rain city behind the grey witch's wagons, twenty-four and head of a company that calls itself the Seventh Day: about 166 cm, slim and wiry. A pair of short horns curling forward from the temples, black with a red glow in them like half-burnt wood, their roots bound with a strip of grey cloth. Black hair cut at the chin. Amber eyes with vertical slit pupils that shine faintly at night. All ten fingertips blackened by gunpowder. Tied round her left upper arm with cord, an old sleeve, once grey and now bleached almost white, marked with seven small grey ink marks. A cold, hard, few-worded air.
face: FACE, as in the references: a young woman's face of about twenty-four, cool and sharp: medium, gently slanted almond eyes of amber with narrow vertical slit pupils and a thin tapering upper lash line; straight black brows; a thin, set mouth. Pale clean skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft warm tone.
build: 166 cm, slim and wiry: a small bust, a narrow waist and slim hips, a callus on the right shoulder from a musket butt.
palette: army grey and powder black, amber, bleached white, ember red
casual: Her company clothes: the grey coat of the seven cities' army with the sleeves rolled to the elbow, dark trousers and boots; slung on her back a single-shot musket cast in the horn city, its stock wrapped in grey cloth; at her belt a powder flask, a bag of lead shot and a short knife; the old bleached sleeve tied twice round her left upper arm. She stands with one hand on the musket's sling, a cold, wary look.
private: On night watch at the boundary stone: the grey coat off, a loose undyed linen shirt with the sleeves rolled, dark trousers and boots, the old sleeve still on her arm. With two blackened fingertips she touches the seven ink marks on the sleeve one by one. A quiet, inward look.
battle: Leading her company across the stones at dawn: the grey army coat buttoned, leather bracers, the powder flask and shot bag at her belt, the old sleeve tied tight. She holds the single-shot musket in both hands, its muzzle low and angled down, ready to raise, a hard, focused look.
formal: Reading names at the prisoner-exchange gate in spring: a long dark grey wool coat buttoned to the top button, as worn before the contract court, the old sleeve tied over its left arm, the grey cloth on her horns newly wound. She holds a written list of names in both hands in front of her, standing very upright, a grave, steady look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the amber slit-pupilled eyes faintly lit, looking at the viewer over the cloth-wrapped stock of a musket. Cold blue night light from one side, the far warm glow of campfires on the other. Foreground blur: drifting powder smoke, the bleached sleeve with its grey marks and a few sparks. She wears the grey army coat with the sleeves rolled.

name: 文策尔·措尔
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:2118
who: Wenzel Zoll, a human, garrison commander of Storkbridge wall-town on the south of the long wall and head of the Zoll family that has kept its gate for generations, fifty-four: about 175 cm, broad-backed and thick-waisted, standing with the feet apart as if nailed to the ground. Hair gone mostly grey, cropped very short; clean-shaven; a notch missing from the left ear where a stray arrow took it. Small pale cornflower-blue eyes, slow and careful. The back of his neck weathered and lined from years of bending over wheat. Big hands with thick knuckles; when he thinks, he licks his right forefinger and holds it up to the wind. On a cord at his neck the big copper key of the exchange gate, rubbed bright. A slow, steady, stubborn air.
face: FACE, as in the references: a square, weathered man's face of about fifty-four, NOT young: lines across the brow and at the eye corners; small pale cornflower-blue eyes, slow and careful; heavy straight grey brows; a closed, patient mouth; clean-shaven; a notch missing from the left ear. Clean skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft warm tone.
build: 175 cm, broad-backed and thick-waisted, solid, the feet planted apart.
palette: grey-brown wool and old mail grey, copper, wheat gold, candle white
casual: His garrison dress: the grey-brown surcoat of Storkbridge wall-town with the sleeves cut a little short for work, over an old shirt of chain mail he never takes off on the wall; dark trousers and boots; a round shield on his back and a short spear at his side, the gate-keeper's gear; the big copper key on its cord at his neck. He holds the short spear low in one hand and raises the licked forefinger of the other to test the wind, a slow, watchful look.
private: At harvest in his strip of wheat nearest the boundary stone: a sweat-darkened undyed linen shirt with the sleeves rolled, rough trousers, boots, a straw hat hanging on his back, the copper key at his neck. He holds a sickle and a water flask. A quiet, contented look.
battle: Standing in the middle of the gateway: the grey-brown surcoat over the old chain mail, an open iron cap, leather gauntlets, the round shield on his left arm, the copper key tucked inside the mail. He holds the short spear forward and low in his right hand, a slow, immovable look.
formal: On the spring day of the prisoner exchange: a clean grey-brown wool coat with plain iron buttons over the old mail, the copper key of the gate at his neck, polished boots. He holds a short lit white candle in both hands in front of him, standing very upright, a grave, quiet look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the small pale blue eyes narrowed into the wind, one licked forefinger raised beside his face. Warm low evening light from one side over a battlement. Foreground blur: wheat ears bending in the wind, the copper key on its cord and a guttering white candle. He wears the grey-brown surcoat over old chain mail.

name: 布洛姆加·炉脉
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:2294
who: Bromgar Forgevein, a dwarf of the Forgevein line and master of the King-Forge at the heart of the forge city, this person in an earlier period: a hundred and fifty-three, before the night of the sinking forge, still with both arms, looking about sixty. Short and enormously broad, about 140 cm, a chest and back as thick as an anvil. A great brown beard in two thick plaits threaded with fire-copper rings, one ring for every piece he has tested and passed. Thick wavy brown hair swept back under a plain iron headband. Steady amber-grey eyes with a white-hot glint like the deepest part of a furnace. Both arms thick as furnace pillars, the right one layered with old spark burns. A gruff, blunt air; he asks about material, use, load and user before saying good or bad.
face: FACE, as in the references: a dwarf man's weathered face of about sixty, broad and heavy, NOT young and NOT a child's: steady amber-grey eyes under bushy brown brows, a few deep lines at their corners; a broad nose; a gruff mouth half hidden by the moustache; a few old scars; no glasses and no lens. Clean skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft warm tone.
build: 140 cm, short and enormously broad: a barrel chest, a back as thick as an anvil, arms thick as furnace pillars and wide hands.
palette: soot brown and blackened leather, white-hot forge yellow, fire copper, a little iron grey
casual: His forge-master's clothes: a heavy leather apron burnt through with countless holes and patched as many times, over a thick wool shirt with the sleeves rolled to the elbow, both burn-scarred forearms bare; dark trousers and iron-capped boots; at his belt a small testing hammer and a rolled drawing of cracks that never leaves him. He holds a long-handled forging hammer handed down from the old forge-master, its head resting on the ground, a gruff, appraising look.
private: At his bench beside the forge at night: the apron off, an old patched wool tunic with the sleeves rolled, soft cloth shoes. He holds a bowl of stew in his left hand, his eyes still turned toward the furnace. A tired, grudgingly warm look.
battle: On the night the King-Forge falters: the burnt apron tied tight over a thick leather jerkin, heavy leather gauntlets, soot on his face, the testing hammer at his belt. He grips the long-handled forging hammer in both hands across his body, a fierce, immovable look.
formal: On the day he took the King-Forge and swore his anvil oath: the same burnt leather apron, brushed, over a clean dark wool coat with copper rivets along its edges, the fire-copper rings in his beard polished; no crown and no jewels. He holds the long-handled forging hammer upright before him in both hands, standing very straight, a grave, steady look.
art: A portrait from slightly below with the camera tilted, the face large, the head cocked as he listens to a furnace wall he has just struck with the small testing hammer, the amber-grey eyes narrowed. White-hot furnace light from one side, hard shadows of the beard braids across his apron. Foreground blur: drifting sparks, a curl of forge smoke and a fire-copper ring on a braid. He wears the burnt and patched leather apron.

name: 托芙
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:2351
who: Tove Deepwell, a dwarf woman of the Deepwell line who goes down the deepest shafts beneath the forge city's royal hall to listen for collapse, sixty-nine and looking about twenty: short, about 129 cm, slight and narrower than other dwarf women, always a little stooped from crawling through wells, as if listening even when she stands straight. Silver-white hair cut at the ears and tied with a bit of well rope. Big ice-blue eyes that shine in the dark and squint in bright light. A grey film of well-dust on her face and the backs of her hands that never washes off; even her eyebrows are grey with it. A clean, beardless face. A quiet, exact air; she always tells you first whether the ground under your feet is solid.
face: FACE, as in the references: a young dwarf woman's face of about twenty, small but grown-up, NOT a child's: big ice-blue almond eyes, a little narrowed, with a thin tapering upper lash line; dust-grey brows; a small nose; a small, serious mouth; a clean, beardless face with a faint grey film of dust on the cheeks; no glasses and no lens. Clean skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft cool tone.
build: 129 cm, small, slight and narrow for a dwarf: a medium bust, a firm waist and rounded hips, a strong back for carrying props down a shaft.
palette: well-dust grey and silver white, ice blue, dark leather, flameless blue-white
casual: Her well-listener's gear: a short dark leather coat of the Deepwell line with thick leather patches at the knees and elbows, dark trousers and soft boots; at her belt a small lamp of cold, flameless blue-white light, a brass listening cone, a small hatchet for splitting props and a coil of well rope. She holds the brass listening cone in one hand, a quiet, attentive look.
private: Above ground for once: a loose grey wool tunic with the sleeves rolled, dark leggings and soft boots, the well-rope tie in her hair. She polishes the glass shade of her flameless lamp with a cloth. A calm, faraway look.
battle: In the hall of the King-Forge on the night it sank: the leather coat buttoned, thick leather gloves, the flameless lamp and the listening cone at her belt, a bundle of wooden props on her back. She grips the prop-splitting hatchet in her right hand, a still, counting look.
formal: On the day the forty-one names were carved: a long dark grey wool dress with long sleeves, a clean leather belt with the listening cone, the hair freshly tied with new well rope. She stands very upright with the hands folded in front, a quiet, solemn look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the ice-blue eyes glowing in darkness, the brass listening cone pressed to a stone wall beside her ear. Cold blue-white light from the flameless lamp below on one side. Foreground blur: drifting stone dust, the grain of a wooden prop and a coil of rope. She wears the patched short leather coat.

name: 弗罗德
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:2407
who: Frode Forgevein, a dwarf, son of the King-Forge master Bromgar, who laid down his hammer at the anvil oath, left home and spent forty-three years keeping thirty-two silent mountain-copper cannons on the long wall at Redforge wall-town, eighty-three and looking about thirty: short and broad, about 145 cm, a little taller than his father and narrower in the shoulders. Sandy-blond hair cut short; a short-trimmed sandy beard with no rings in it, against his clan's custom; amber-grey eyes like his father's. Old soot from the cannons' fire channels ground into both hands; an old burn scar across his left palm from pulling a door latch out of a furnace when he was ten. A quiet, slow, careful air; he would rather keep a thing than make one.
face: FACE, as in the references: a dwarf man's face of about thirty, broad and quiet, NOT a child's and NOT old: amber-grey eyes, steady and a little guarded; short sandy brows; a straight nose; a closed, careful mouth framed by a short-trimmed sandy beard; no glasses and no lens. Clean skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft warm tone.
build: 145 cm, short and broad, narrower in the shoulders than a forge smith, sturdy enough to crawl through fire channels.
palette: old leather brown and soot black, mountain-copper bronze, sandy blond, ember red
casual: His cannon-keeper's clothes: the old leather coat of the wall-town guards, its cuffs scorched in a few places, over a dark wool shirt, dark trousers and heavy boots; at his waist a ring of thirty-two iron keys, one for each cannon door. He holds an oiled rag, about to wipe a cannon's bore, a quiet, careful look.
private: In the bake-room of the wall-town before dawn: the leather coat off, a loose undyed linen shirt with the sleeves rolled, flour on his sooty hands. He holds a round loaf he is breaking in half for the sentry on the wall. A shy, quiet look.
battle: On the night of the re-forging on the wall: the old leather coat belted over a thick leather apron, heavy leather gloves, the ring of keys at his waist. He grips a forging hammer taken from the old rack of the Redforge house in his right hand, a tense, determined look.
formal: On the morning the thirty-two cannons were raised: the guards' grey-brown surcoat brushed clean over the old leather coat, the ring of keys polished at his belt, polished boots. He stands very upright with the hands at his sides, a solemn, quiet look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the amber-grey eyes looking at the viewer from inside a narrow stone channel, soot on one cheek. Red ember light glowing along the channel from one side. Foreground blur: a ring of iron keys, drifting soot and the round bronze rim of a cannon mouth. He wears the old leather coat with scorched cuffs.

name: 巴纳比·篷灯
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:2671
who: Barnaby Lampwagon, a halfling of a wagon family that has run the middle of the long wall for generations, and for nearly fifty years a White Candle healer who drives one cart back and forth through the fallen gate to dress the wounds of both sides, sixty-eight and looking like a human man in his early fifties: short and round, about 112 cm, with a belly. A red face, deep lines at the eye corners, small hazel eyes that close to slits when he laughs. Curly grey-white hair, a few white hairs on the tips of his pointed ears. Short thick hands covered in needle pricks and burn scars. He walks a little splay-footed. A talkative, food-loving, nosy and kindly air; he never passes on a secret.
face: FACE, as in the references: a halfling man's face of about fifty, round and ruddy, NOT a child's: small hazel eyes creased with laugh lines, deep lines at their corners; bushy grey-white brows; a round nose; a wide, talkative mouth. Clean skin with very little shading, the cheeks warm red; skin shadows a soft warm tone.
build: 112 cm, short and round, with a belly, short thick arms and big hands.
palette: White Candle grey-white, soup brown, candle gold, wagon wood, ruddy red
casual: His White Candle travelling dress: a grey-white long robe, the front stained with medicine and soup until no one can tell which is which, the sleeves rolled; a cloth bag at his waist holding needles, thread, splints, a jar of bear fat and a pouch of salt; sturdy boots worn thicker on one side. He holds up a small lantern with a white candle burning in it, the lamp of his cart, a warm, chatty smile.
private: At his cart's cooking pot: the robe's sleeves tied back, a stained cook's apron over it, the curly hair untidy. He holds a ladle in one hand and a wooden bowl of bean soup in the other, about to hand it over. A cheerful, coaxing grin.
battle: Going among the wounded on both sides of the wall: the grey-white robe belted short, the sleeves tied back, a canvas satchel of bandages and splints across his body, a folding table strapped to his back. He holds a roll of bandage in one hand and the white-candle lantern in the other.
battle_pose: 3) the field outfit: braced and steady, the feet a little apart, a serious, unsmiling expression, holding a roll of bandage in one hand and a small white-candle lantern in the other, a folding table strapped to his back; he carries no weapon.
formal: On the last night of the year at the boundary stone: a freshly washed grey-white White Candle robe, a clean white stole over the shoulders, the curly hair combed. He holds a lit white candle in a small brass holder in both hands in front of him, standing very upright, a quiet, hopeful look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the eyes creased into a laughing smile, a wooden bowl of steaming soup held up toward the viewer. Warm golden candle light from a lantern on one side against a cold night. Foreground blur: rising steam, the flame of a white candle and the edge of a wooden folding table. He wears the stained grey-white White Candle robe.

name: 莉妮·穆勒
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:3799
who: Linnie Muller, a girl of the mill family of Watermill village behind the south of the long wall, nine years old, small for her age and wholly covered by her clothes. When she sleeps, whoever sleeps in the same room dreams her dream, mostly of the water wheel, of flour and of her father. Her head was shaved at the blood-cleansing house in the mountains, and until her hair grows back she wears a soft cloth cap her mother sewed, a little wheat-blond stubble showing at the nape. Clear sky-blue eyes, often half closed as if drowsy. A quiet, sleepy, trusting air.
palette: flour white and undyed linen, mill blue, wheat gold, sky blue
casual: Back home at the mill: a plain long-sleeved linen dress to the shins, a small flour-dusted apron, wool stockings and little wooden-soled shoes, the soft cloth cap her mother sewed pulled down over her shaved head. She holds a handful of wheat grain cupped in both hands, a shy, sleepy smile.
private: At bedtime in the mill house: a long undyed flannel nightgown with long sleeves, thick socks, the cloth cap still on. She hugs a small pillow, the eyes half closed. A drowsy look.
battle: The days of the court on the black stone terrace: a too-big grey coat from the blood-cleansing house wrapped round her, the shaved head bare, small shoes.
battle_pose: 3) the outfit of the court days: standing small and still, the feet together, a quiet, watchful expression, both hands holding the edges of a too-big grey coat closed at her collar; she does not fight.
formal: At the harvest feast in Watermill: a clean blue wool dress with long sleeves and a white collar, a new cloth cap with an embroidered band, polished little shoes. She holds a small bag of new flour in both arms, standing very straight, a shy, proud look.
art: A head-and-shoulders portrait, the face turned slightly, the sky-blue eyes half closed and dreamy, a haze of drifting flour around her. Soft warm morning light from a mill window on one side. Foreground blur: drifting flour, the wooden paddles of a water wheel and a few wheat grains. She wears the soft cloth cap and the plain linen dress, closed at the collar.

name: 博尼法斯
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:3802
who: Bonifaz, a human, head stone-keeper of the blood-cleansing house in the eastern mountains, a converted cloister where children whose blood was judged to carry demon fire were kept and tested each month, head of the house for thirty years and seventy-four years old: tall and thin, about 182 cm, a little stooped. Long white eyebrows that hang down over his eyes; close-cropped white hair. Pale blue eyes half hidden under the brows. He speaks one word at a time, as if reciting a prayer. A grave, certain air; he believes in what he has done.
face: FACE, as in the references: a long, thin old man's face of about seventy-four, NOT young: long white eyebrows hanging down over pale blue eyes; deep lines across the brow and beside the mouth; a long nose; a thin, solemn mouth; clean-shaven; no glasses. Clean skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft cool tone.
build: about 182 cm, tall and thin, a little stooped.
palette: washed grey and white stone, pale blue, needle silver, dark wood
casual: The house's grey robe: a long washed-out grey robe with a small white stone pinned at the collar, a plain cord belt, soft shoes; at his waist a flat wooden case holding silver needles and a stack of small white stones. He stands with the hands folded into his sleeves, a grave, certain look.
private: In his cell in the stone house: a plain grey wool tunic, a dark shawl over the shoulders, soft shoes. He holds an old leather-bound register of names, closed, against his chest. A quiet, weary look.
battle: Riding to the court on the black stone terrace: the grey robe under a heavy grey travelling cloak with the hood thrown back, riding boots, the white stone at the collar. He holds the flat wooden case of needles and stones in both hands.
battle_pose: 3) the travelling outfit: upright and stern, the feet together, a severe expression, holding the flat wooden case of needles and white stones in both hands; he does not fight.
formal: Before the court on the obsidian terrace: the grey robe washed clean, a long white stole embroidered with small grey stones along its edges, the white stone at the collar. He stands very upright with the hands folded, a solemn, certain look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the long white brows shadowing the pale blue eyes, one thin hand pressed flat on a small grey-white stone seal. Cold grey light from a high window on one side. Foreground blur: a silver needle, a small white stone with a dark spot on it and drifting dust. He wears the washed-out grey robe with the white stone at the collar.

name: 洛伦兹·克兰茨
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:3836
who: Lorenz Kranz, a human, garrison commander of Swallownest wall-town in the middle of the long wall, who has held this stretch of wall for over forty years, sixty-eight: tall, about 184 cm, lean, his back now bent with the stoop of a man who has stood too long on battlements. Close-cropped white hair; a lean, lined face; deep-set pale hazel eyes. Big knotted hands. He speaks slowly, one sentence to one order, and never takes an order back. A grave, tired, rule-bound air; he knows which way the wind is blowing and gives the order anyway.
face: FACE, as in the references: a lean, lined old man's face of about sixty-eight, NOT young: deep-set pale hazel eyes under heavy white brows, deep lines at their corners and across the brow; a long nose; a thin, grave mouth; clean-shaven. Clean skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft warm tone.
build: about 184 cm, tall and lean, the back stooped.
palette: wall grey and old bronze, white, mail grey, beacon orange
casual: His garrison commander's coat: a long wall-grey wool officer's coat buttoned up over an old mail shirt, a plain old-bronze clasp at the collar marking his command, a broad leather belt with a sword, dark trousers and boots, a heavy grey cloak over the shoulders. He rests one big hand on the sword hilt, a grave, tired look.
private: In his room in the south gate tower: a plain undyed wool shirt, a dark wool waistcoat, grey trousers and soft shoes. He holds a cup of hot water, looking past it. A tired, worried look.
battle: On the south gate tower the night of the fire: a mail shirt and a dented iron breastplate over the grey coat, an open-faced iron helm, gauntlets, a round shield on his left arm. He holds his drawn sword point down, a hard, grave look.
formal: At the stele of the burnt wheat on the first day of the harvest: the grey officer's coat brushed and buttoned to the throat, the old-bronze collar clasp polished, a dark sash, white gloves, the sword at his side. He stands as straight as his back allows, the hands folded on the sword pommel, a grave, quiet look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the pale hazel eyes looking past the viewer toward a fire, the mouth set. Orange firelight from one side against a night sky. Foreground blur: drifting embers, smoke and the stone edge of a battlement. He wears the long grey officer's coat with the old-bronze collar clasp.

name: 罗兰德·布兰肯
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:3837
who: Roland Blanken, a human knight, second son of the Blanken house of the duchies, twenty-four and serving his year on the wall at Swallownest: tall, about 185 cm, broad-shouldered. Bright honey-gold hair worn to the collar and combed with care; warm green eyes. His armour was made by his family's own smiths and is polished so bright that the soldiers call him Shiny-Plate behind his back. Restless and eager, sour that a whole year on the wall has not seen a single arrow fly. His arrows are fletched with white goose feathers bound with a ring of red thread, as the knightly houses of the duchies do it.
build: 185 cm, tall, broad-shouldered and trained.
palette: mirror-polished steel and honey gold, duchy white, thread red, leaf green
casual: His dress on the wall: a padded white arming doublet with the polished breastplate and pauldrons buckled over it even off duty, dark breeches, polished riding boots, a sword at his hip. He rests one hand on the sword hilt, an impatient, eager look.
private: In the stables at night: a loose white linen shirt, a dark waistcoat, breeches and boots, gloves tucked in his belt. He holds a polishing cloth and a gauntlet he is buffing to a shine. A bored, sulky look.
battle: Ready to ride out of the south gate: his family's full plate polished to a mirror shine, a short white surcoat over it, an open-faced helm, a quiver of white-fletched arrows at his hip. He grips his drawn longsword in both hands, point low, a hot, eager look.
formal: In his family's hall in the duchies: a long white wool coat with the Blanken arms embroidered small at the breast, a red sash, white gloves, polished boots, the hair combed. He stands very straight with one hand on the sword hilt, a proud, slightly sullen look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the warm green eyes glaring past the viewer toward a fire, the polished pauldron throwing back the hot light. Orange firelight from one side at night. Foreground blur: an arrow fletched with white goose feathers bound in red thread, drifting smoke and sparks. He wears the polished breastplate over the white arming doublet.

name: 梅蒂·雨歇
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:3839
who: Meti Rainrest, a tiefling border officer of the black empire who keeps the contracts of Wheatshed village and the villages beside it west of the boundary stones, fifty and looking just over thirty: small and thin, about 155 cm. A pair of short horns lying back flat against the scalp. Dusk-violet hair cut at the jaw. Light green eyes. A soft voice and careful, exact accounts. A quiet, steady, unflinching air; on the night the wheat burned she walked out alone in front of an armed camp and stood with her back to the boundary stone.
build: about 155 cm, small and thin.
palette: contract black and dark red, dusk violet, light green, ink brown
casual: Her border officer's dress: a long black wool coat of the western cut buttoned to the throat, a narrow dark red sash, a small bronze plate on the left shoulder engraved with her post's contract mark, dark trousers and boots; at her belt a leather case holding the rolled contracts of her villages. She holds a small account book open in one hand and a pencil in the other, a quiet, careful look.
private: At her desk in the border post: a long-sleeved plum wool dress, a dark knitted shawl, soft shoes. She holds a cup of tea, a pen still between her fingers. A tired, gentle look.
battle: The night of the burnt wheat: the black coat buttoned to the throat, the red sash, a smear of soot on her cheek, the contract case at her belt.
battle_pose: 3) the night outfit: standing alone and very straight, the feet planted, a calm, unflinching expression, both empty hands open at her sides; she carries no weapon.
formal: At the contract court for the reading of a judgement: a long dark grey wool coat buttoned to the top button, the bronze contract plate on its shoulder, a dark red sash. She holds the rolled contract case in both hands in front of her, a grave, composed look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the light green eyes steady, her back against a grey boundary stone with a lantern burning on top of it. Red firelight from one side against the night. Foreground blur: drifting ash, the glow of the lantern and the curled edge of a contract scroll. She wears the long black border officer's coat.

name: 卢瑟·施奈德
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:3841
who: Luther Schneider, a human stonemason of the Stonecutters' Street line who looks after the boundary stones along several stretches of the long wall, walking the wall every autumn to recut letters worn shallow, fifty-one: about 176 cm, solid and square. Grey hair cropped short; slate-blue eyes; a fine dust of stone in the creases of his knuckles. Hands with calluses harder than the stone he cuts. A man of few words, patient and exact; he reads a stone before he reads a face.
face: FACE, as in the references: a square, weathered man's face of about fifty, NOT young: slate-blue eyes, steady, with lines at their corners; short grey brows; a broad nose; a closed, patient mouth; a short grey stubble. Clean skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft warm tone.
build: about 176 cm, solid and square-built, with big callused hands.
palette: grey canvas and stone dust, iron, leather brown, slate blue
casual: His mason's working clothes: grey canvas work clothes with the knees and elbows patched with two layers of leather, a wide leather belt hung with a row of chisels of every size, a mallet and a chalk line, heavy boots. He holds a chisel and a mallet, a quiet, exact look.
private: At home in a wall-town to the south: a plain undyed wool shirt with the sleeves rolled, a dark wool waistcoat, grey trousers, soft shoes. He holds a small piece of stone, turning it to read the grain. A calm look.
battle: On the road along the wall in autumn: the grey canvas clothes under a heavy grey work coat, a leather apron, a pack of tools on his back.
battle_pose: 3) the working outfit: braced and steady, the feet planted, a focused expression, holding a chisel against an unseen stone in one hand and a raised mallet in the other; he does not fight.
formal: At the setting of a new stele: a clean dark grey wool coat buttoned up over a white shirt collar, the chisels left at home, polished boots. He stands very upright with the hands folded in front, a grave look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the slate-blue eyes narrowed at a worn letter on a stone beside his face, a chisel set against it. Cold autumn light from one side. Foreground blur: drifting stone dust, the grain of grey stone and an arrow with white fletching bound in red thread. He wears the grey canvas work clothes.

name: 齐亚德
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:3855
who: Ziyad, a fire-horn demon-kin, head of the Horn-Crown house of the Charred-Gate clan, which kept the empty high seat of the city-burner for two hundred and sixty-five years, about four hundred and sixteen and looking about sixty: tall, his back bent with age. Two horns curving back from the temples in two half-circles, a ring of black obsidian clasped round each root, the tips burnt black, blacker than anyone's in his clan. Skin with a faint red cast. Iron-grey hair with the last of its dark red at the nape, tied back. Red-gold eyes like his granddaughter's. Big hands with thick knuckles whose palms are always hot. A slow, low-voiced, courteous air; he speaks only of rules and of what is owed.
face: FACE, as in the references: an old man's face of about sixty, long and lined, NOT young: red-gold eyes under heavy brows, deep lines at their corners; a long straight nose; a thin, courteous mouth; clean-shaven. Clean skin with a faint warm red cast and very little shading; skin shadows a soft warm red-brown.
build: tall and long-limbed, the back bent with age, big knuckled hands.
palette: charred black and obsidian, dull ember red, iron grey, ash white
casual: His clan head's clothes: a long black leather coat of the Charred-Gate cut, the cuffs clasped with iron rings, over a dark red wool robe, a wide black sash, soft boots; at his waist a short, heavy, broad-bladed knife in a plain sheath. He stands with the hot hands clasped behind his bent back, a courteous, unreadable look.
private: In the long hall of the clan camp: a loose dark red wool robe, a black shawl, soft shoes. He holds an account book of the valley's black-stone trade, open, its pages neat. A quiet, courteous look.
battle: On the grey ridge at dawn: the black leather coat with the iron-ringed cuffs over a dark breastplate, the obsidian rings on his horns polished. He grips the short, heavy, broad-bladed knife in his right hand, a cold, patient look.
formal: Presiding at the clan's rites: a long black robe to the floor with a high collar, the hem embroidered with small flame-and-gate shapes in dark red, a heavy iron chain of office across the shoulders, the obsidian rings on his horns polished. He stands as straight as his back allows, the hot hands folded in front, a grave, courteous look.
art: A portrait from slightly below with the camera tilted, the face large, the red-gold eyes looking down at the viewer with a courteous, cold calm, one big hand raised near his chest. Grey dawn light from one side over a ridge of ash. Foreground blur: drifting ash, the shadow of a heavy chain and the burnt black tip of a horn. He wears the long black leather coat with the iron-ringed cuffs.

name: 赫尔弗里德·银鹿
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:3876
who: Helfried Silverstag, a human knight, nephew of the Duke of Silverstag in the Iris duchies, a hero-rank warrior who leads twenty-one thousand of the duchy's soldiers to the south of the long wall, thirty-eight: tall, about 186 cm, broad-shouldered and trim. Pale gold hair combed neatly back; a short beard trimmed with great precision; ice-blue eyes. Polite to the point of chill. At his hip a long-barrelled casting-gun, a spell implement shaped like a gun, its barrel engraved with fine spell circuits and fitted with a crystal chamber cased in silver, carved by a great mage of the Arcane Association as a gift to his uncle; before speaking of it, he always names the mage. A courteous, cold, assured air.
build: about 186 cm, tall, broad-shouldered and trim.
palette: silver and duchy green, pale gold, ice blue, a little white
casual: His knight's camp dress: a fitted dark green riding coat with silver buttons and a small silver stag embroidered at the breast, a white shirt, a dark sash, pale buff breeches, tall black riding boots, white gloves; at his hip in a fine holster the engraved casting-gun with its silver crystal chamber. One gloved hand rests on the gun's grip, a polite, chilly smile.
private: In his pavilion at night: a white linen shirt open at the throat, a dark green waistcoat, dark breeches and soft boots. He holds a silver cup of wine. A relaxed, faintly amused look.
battle: Leading his knights down a rope over the wall at night: silver-edged dark steel half-plate with a silver stag on the breastplate, a dark green cloak, gauntlets. He holds the casting-gun low in one hand, its silver crystal chamber glowing faintly, a cool, intent look.
formal: At the duke's court: a long dark green coat with silver embroidery of stag antlers along its edges, a high white collar, a silver chain of his house across the chest, white gloves, polished boots, the casting-gun left behind. He stands very straight with one hand on a dress sword, a courteous, cold look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the ice-blue eyes looking at the viewer over a polite, chilly smile. Warm campfire light from one side, cold night on the other. Foreground blur: the silver crystal glow of the casting-gun's chamber, a silver stag clasp and drifting embers. He wears the dark green riding coat with the silver stag.

name: 塞昆达
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:3877
who: Secunda, a demon-kin of the white-bone folk, born so and never dead, border officer of the black empire on the Storkbridge stretch of the wall, who has stood at the outer end of the exchange gateway and read the names every spring for nearly sixty years, about a hundred and eighty-nine and looking about sixty: tall and thin, about 176 cm, with long fingers. Very pale skin; the bone shows white and gleaming at her cheekbones, along her jaw and at every knuckle. Silver-white hair in a low knot. Pale violet eyes. On her left arm a round shield of bone. A steady, even voice that has never got a name wrong. A dry, composed, quietly kind air.
face: FACE, as in the references: a woman's face of about sixty, long and calm, NOT young: pale violet eyes, steady, with fine lines at their corners; thin silver brows; the cheekbones and the line of the jaw showing as smooth white bone through the pale skin; a composed, thin mouth. Very pale clean skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft cool grey.
build: about 176 cm, tall and thin, long-fingered, straight-backed.
palette: bone white and pale violet, contract black, silver white, candle gold
casual: Her border officer's dress: a long black wool coat of the western cut buttoned to the throat, a narrow dark red sash, a small bronze plate on the left shoulder engraved with her post's contract mark, dark trousers and boots; the round bone shield on her left arm. Her long right hand rests at her sash, a composed, watchful look.
private: At the border post after the reading: a long grey wool dress buttoned to the throat, a dark shawl, soft shoes, the shield set aside. She holds a cup of water in both bony hands, resting her voice. A quiet, tired look.
battle: Holding the gateway: the black coat belted tight, leather bracers, the round bone shield raised on her left arm, an iron-shod staff in her right hand. A calm, unmoving look.
formal: On the spring day of the exchange: the black coat buttoned to the throat with a white sash, the bone shield on her arm. She holds the list of names open in both hands in front of her, standing very upright, a grave, steady look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the pale violet eyes lowered to a list of names she is reading aloud, the white bone of her cheekbone catching the light. Warm candle light from one side in a stone gateway. Foreground blur: the flame of a white candle, the curved rim of a bone shield and drifting dust. She wears the long black border officer's coat.

name: 穆尼尔
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:3878
who: Munir, a fire-horn demon-kin contract farmer of Bridgewest village beyond the boundary stones at Storkbridge, eighty-one: about 178 cm, lean and wiry, his hair gone white but his back still straight. A pair of short horns curving back from the temples, worn dull with age. Skin with a warm red-brown cast. Ember-orange eyes. On the inside of his left wrist five old knife scars, each fainter than the last, cut by the blood collectors of the old high seats before the first law was carved; his granddaughter's wrists have none. A wooden contract tag at his belt. A calm, plain-spoken, unafraid old man.
face: FACE, as in the references: an old man's face of about eighty, lean and lined, NOT young: ember-orange eyes, calm, with deep lines at their corners; thick white brows; a straight nose; a closed, steady mouth; clean-shaven. Clean skin with a warm red-brown cast and very little shading; skin shadows a soft warm brown.
build: about 178 cm, lean and wiry, the back still straight.
palette: undyed linen and earth brown, ash white, ember orange, wheat gold
casual: His contract-folk clothes: a coarse undyed linen shirt with the sleeves rolled to the forearm, the five scars bare on the left wrist, a hemp-rope belt with a small wooden tag branded with his family's contract number, rough brown trousers and worn boots. He holds a short hoe over one shoulder, a calm, plain look.
private: At home in Bridgewest: the plain grey wool coat issued to the contract-folk each winter, over the linen shirt, soft shoes. He holds a wooden bowl of porridge in both hands. A quiet, warm look.
battle: The morning he was taken over the wall: the linen shirt untucked, the grey winter coat thrown over his shoulders, the left sleeve pushed back over the scarred wrist.
battle_pose: 3) the outfit of the morning he was taken: standing very straight and unafraid, the feet a little apart, a calm, steady expression, both hands open at his sides; he does not fight.
formal: At the exchange gate in spring: a clean dark grey wool coat buttoned to the top button, as worn before the contract court, the wooden contract tag on its cord outside the coat, clean boots. He stands very upright with the hands folded in front, a quiet, dignified look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the ember-orange eyes looking at the viewer calmly, the left sleeve pushed back so the five faint scars on the wrist show beside his face. Cold grey dawn light from one side. Foreground blur: drifting wheat chaff, a white candle flame and the edge of a stone gateway. He wears the coarse undyed linen shirt.

name: 约伦·无炉
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:3887
who: Jorun Hearthless, a dwarf of no line from the reed-hut slums of the golden-kite city, who has baked bread in the oven room of Redforge wall-town for over a hundred and sixty years, three hundred and forty-six and looking like a human woman of about sixty: short and stocky, about 138 cm, broad-shouldered. Two thick braids, once ginger and now mostly white, coiled on top of her head. A round face, a big nose red at the tip, small bright amber eyes; flour always on her face and on her eyebrows. Thick red hands, scar laid over scar from a lifetime of burns. On one wrist a cord tied in a knot by an old friend, with more knots added since. A clean, beardless face. A short-spoken, bossy, warm air; she feeds people before she lets them talk.
face: FACE, as in the references: a dwarf woman's face of about sixty, round and ruddy, NOT a child's: small bright amber eyes with deep laugh lines at the corners; floury white brows; a big round nose red at the tip; a wide, no-nonsense mouth; a clean, beardless face; no glasses and no lens. Clean skin with very little shading, the cheeks warm red; skin shadows a soft warm tone.
build: 138 cm, short and stocky: broad shoulders, a full bust, a thick waist and broad hips, strong arms for kneading.
palette: flour white and ginger going white, oilcloth olive, oven yellow, a little cord red
casual: Her baker's clothes: an oilcloth apron with burn holes patched on the front, over a long brown wool dress with the sleeves rolled to the elbow all year round; at her waist a long-handled iron ladle, a pouch of salt and a kitchen knife; the knotted cord on her wrist. She holds the long wooden baking peel upright at her side, its blade resting on the floor, a bossy, warm look.
private: After the night's baking: the apron dusted with flour, the sleeves rolled, flour everywhere. She holds out a round, hard-crusted loaf in both hands. A gruff, kindly look.
battle: On the night the cold furnace heart was lit again: the oilcloth apron tied tight, a cloth tied over the braids, soot on her face.
battle_pose: 3) the night-of-the-furnace outfit: braced and fierce, the feet planted wide, a hard, set expression, holding a long wooden baking peel in both hands with a heap of glowing yellow embers on its blade, ready to throw them into a furnace; she does not fight.
formal: Her cleanest clothes, worn only when someone makes her: a dark green wool dress with long sleeves, a fresh white apron over it, the white braids newly coiled, most of the flour brushed from her brows. She stands very upright with the hands folded over the apron, an impatient, dignified look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the small amber eyes looking at the viewer with a gruff, warm look, one floury hand pressed flat against an iron oven door as if testing its heat. Warm yellow oven light from one side. Foreground blur: drifting flour, a few yellow sparks and the crust of a round loaf. She wears the patched oilcloth apron.

name: 兰维格
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:3905
who: Ranveig, the old matriarch of the Forgevein line and once master of the King-Forge, who taught three masters of the forge to read the furnace, three hundred and forty and looking like a human woman in her early seventies: a dwarf woman, short, about 132 cm, grown thin with age, the shoulders still square. A long white beard braided into plaits threaded with dozens of fire-copper rings, one ring for each piece she has tested and passed, more rings than anyone in the forge city; white hair drawn back tightly. Washed-out blue eyes. The backs of both hands layered with old burn scars. Deaf in the left ear from the furnace, she turns her right side toward anyone who speaks. A slow, low-voiced, unbending air; she asks about the thing in your hands, not about you.
face: FACE, as in the references: an old dwarf woman's face of about seventy, NOT young: deep lines at the eyes and across the brow; washed-out blue eyes, calm and sharp; thin white brows; a broad nose; a firm old mouth half hidden by a long white beard braided with fire-copper rings; clearly a woman and NOT a man; no glasses and no lens. Clean skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft warm tone.
build: about 132 cm, short and thin for a dwarf, the shoulders still square.
palette: white and fire copper, soot black, faded wool brown, forge glow
casual: Her old forge-master's clothes: a long soot-dark wool dress with the sleeves rolled to the elbow, a heavy scorched leather apron over it, a thick knitted shawl over the shoulders, sturdy old boots; a small testing hammer at her belt. She holds the small testing hammer up near her right ear, a slow, listening look.
private: At the door of her house in the royal hall: a loose old wool robe, a thick shawl, soft felt shoes. She holds a small cup of something hot in both scarred hands. A calm, stubborn look.
battle: In the royal hall on the night it sank: the scorched apron tied over the wool dress, the shawl knotted, heavy leather gloves tucked in the belt, the testing hammer in her hand.
battle_pose: 3) the last-night outfit: steady and unmoving, the feet planted, a calm, stubborn expression, holding a small testing hammer in one hand and facing forward; she does not fight.
formal: As the old matriarch at an anvil oath: a long black wool robe with fire-copper rivets along its hem, the scorched apron left off, every ring in her beard polished, the white hair bound with a plain copper band. She stands very upright with the hands folded over the testing hammer, a grave, proud look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the old face turned so the right ear is toward the viewer, listening, the washed-out blue eyes half closed. White furnace light from one side, glinting on dozens of copper rings in her beard. Foreground blur: drifting sparks, forge smoke and a small hammer. She wears the scorched leather apron over the soot-dark wool dress.

name: 阿托·雾耕
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_六_麦的年月.md:3928
who: Ato Mistplough, a younger version of this person: a tiefling boy of the contract-folk village called Ninety-Three beyond the boundary stones, Kaya's little brother, eight years old and looking seven, wholly covered by his clothes. Short curly hair of a mist blue a shade paler than his sister's. Two small bumps at the temples where his horns are only just breaking through. Pale yellow eyes that glow a little in the dark. Fair skin, the cheeks red from the fog. He clutches the small copper bell of the black goat he watched being born. A cheerful, stubborn, chattering air; he insists he heard someone crying down in the crack.
face: FACE, as in the references: a tiefling child's face of about seven, round and bright: large pale yellow eyes with a faint glow and a thin tapering upper lash line; short pale blue brows; a tiny nose; a small, chattering mouth; soft round cheeks reddened by fog; two small bumps at the temples where horns are just breaking through. Clean skin with very little shading; skin shadows a soft warm tone.
palette: mist blue and pale yellow, faded homespun brown, sheep's-wool cream, copper
casual: His shepherd-boy clothes: a faded homespun tunic to the knees with long sleeves, belted with a cord, wool leggings, small boots mended at the toes, a sheepskin vest with the fleece inside, a short shepherd's stick tucked under one arm. He holds the small copper goat bell in one hand, a bright, chattering look.
private: At home in the farmhouse on a foggy evening: a long undyed wool shirt, thick knitted socks, a blanket round his shoulders. He holds a small wooden bowl of warm milk in both hands. A sleepy, contented look.
battle: The evening he fell into the crack: the homespun tunic smeared with earth, one boot lost, a rope tied round his waist.
battle_pose: 3) the outfit of that evening: shaken but standing, the feet a little apart, a stubborn, wide-eyed expression, clutching the small copper goat bell close in both hands, a rope tied round his waist; he does not fight.
formal: The last night of the year at the boundary stone: a clean dark blue wool coat a size too big, buttoned to the chin, a knitted cap pulled over the horn buds, small boots. He stands very straight with the hands clasped in front, a solemn, sleepy look.
art: A head-and-shoulders portrait, the face turned slightly, the pale yellow eyes glowing softly through fog, the small copper goat bell held up near his cheek as if listening to it. Cold white fog light from one side. Foreground blur: thick drifting fog, a goat bell's cord and a few blades of grass. He wears the homespun tunic and the sheepskin vest, closed at the collar.
